title: Level sets, contours, and quadric surfaces
section: Analytic Geometry of R3 ▷ Level Curves and Level Surfaces
terms: level curve; level surface; contour curve; cross-section; circular paraboloid; elliptic paraboloid; hyperboloid of one sheet.

exposition.text:
2
The level set of f at value c is {p : f (p) = c}. For f : R → R it is usually a curve, and for
3
f : R → R usually a surface, but it may be empty, a point, or singular. A contour of the graph
z = f(x, y) at height c is its intersection with z = c; projecting this contour to the xy-plane
gives the level curve.
2 2 2 2
Quadrics are recognized through cross-sections. The elliptic paraboloid z = x /a + y /b has
2 2 2 2 2 2
elliptic horizontal sections. The one-sheet hyperboloid x /a + y /b − z /c = 1 has nonempty
2 2 2 2
elliptic sections at every height. A sphere satisfies (x − a) + (y − b) + (z − c) = R . For
2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2
comparison, z = x + y is a circular double cone, and z /c − x /a − y /b = 1 is a two-sheet
hyperboloid, with sections only for |z| ≥ c.
The elliptic paraboloid becomes a circular paraboloid when a = b. Its zero-height level is a
point, positive-height levels are ellipses (circles when a = b), and negative-height levels are
empty. A circular double cone has two nappes meeting at its vertex; unlike a two-sheet hyper-
boloid, it is connected through that vertex.

For f(x, y) = x − y , which description of the level set f (0) is correct?
(A) A point
(B) A circle
(C) One straight line
(D) Two intersecting straight lines
(E) A hyperbola with two disjoint branches

solution.text:
2 2
The equation x − y = (x − y)(x + y) = 0 is the union of y = x and y = −x. Nonzero levels
are hyperbolas, but the zero level is degenerate.

For the graph z = x + 4y , which pair correctly gives the level curve of value 9 and its contour
in three-dimensional space?
2 2 2
(A) x + 4y = 9 in R ; the same ellipse at z = 9
2 2 2
(B) x + 4y = 9 in R ; the same ellipse at z = 0
2 2 2
(C) x + 4y = 81 in R ; the same ellipse at z = 9
2 2 2
(D) x + y = 9 in R ; a circle at z = 9
(E) The single point (0, 0); the point (0, 0, 9)

solution.text:
The level curve is the set of inputs where f (x, y) = 9, namely an ellipse with semiaxes 3
and 3/2. The contour consists of graph points (x, y, 9) above that ellipse. A level curve
lives in the input plane; its graph contour retains the output height.

Which level set of f(x, y) = x + y − 4x + 6y is a single point?
−1 −1 −1 −1 −1
(A) f (0) (B) f (13) (C) f (−14) (D) f (−13) (E) f (−12)

solution.text:
2 2
Completing squares gives f = (x − 2) + (y +3) − 13. The minimum level −13 consists solely
of (2, −3); lower levels are empty and higher levels are circles.

For which real c does the level surface (x − 1) + (y + 2) + (z − 3) = c meet the plane z = 0 in
exactly one point?
(A) c = 0 (B) c = 3 (C) c = 9 (D) c > 9 (E) c ≥ 9

solution.text:
2 2
On z = 0 the equation becomes (x − 1) + (y + 2) = c − 9. It is empty for c < 9, a sin-
gle point for c = 9, and a circle for c > 9. This includes the distinction between a spherical
level surface and its potentially degenerate planar section.
